name: estate-corridor-night-verify-off
description: ESTATE-CORRIDOR-NIGHT — the BEFORE arm: same scenario as estate-corridor-night-verify.json but forces estateCorridorNightMask OFF. Estate.tsx's `materials()` is a MODULE-LEVEL SINGLETON built lazily on the FIRST call and never rebuilt (`if (!mats) mats = buildMaterials(...)`), and `Estate`/`EstateGeometry` mount essentially at boot (default cameraMode is orbit, `estateSurround` defaults on) — i.e. before any post-load `setup` eval step can run. A `setFeatureFlag` call in `setup` (the glazingLightmapExclude-off pattern) therefore arrives too late here: verified live (see report) that it leaves the NEW mask baked in regardless. The flag must instead be forced off via the URL query override (`?ff=estateCorridorNightMask:off`, parsed synchronously at store-module load, before the first React render) — run this scenario with `SHOT_URL` including that query string, e.g. `SHOT_URL="http://localhost:5200/?ff=estateCorridorNightMask:off"` (SHOT_URL takes precedence over this file's own `url` field, per shot.mjs's own precedence rule, so the query must be on whichever one actually reaches the browser). The `setFeatureFlag` call in `setup` below is kept as a harmless no-op reinforcement, not the real mechanism. Reproduces the legacy corridor mask: a full-height gradient filling the whole corridor void, the defect the orchestrator saw. Run with SHOT_GPU=1 and img-diff each numbered screenshot against the matching one from estate-corridor-night-verify.json.

steps.name: setup
steps.eval: (() => { try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.(); s.dismissChecklist?.(); s.setFeatureFlag?.('estateCorridorNightMask', false); s.setManualHour?.(20); s.setTimeMode?.('manual'); s.setLightsMode?.('on'); s.setQualityTier?.('realistic'); s.setDeviceClass?.('capable'); s.hideLoading?.(); s.setFeatureFlag?.('interactiveDegrade', false) })()

steps.name: pin-device-class
steps.eval: (() => { const s = window.__store; s.getState().setDeviceClass('capable'); s.setState({ setDeviceClass: () => {} }) })()

steps.name: pose-yard-night
steps.eval: (() => { const l = window.__walkLook; l.setPosition(5.42, 7.6); l.setYaw(Math.PI); l.setPitch(-0.1) })()

steps.name: pose-living-night
steps.eval: (() => { const l = window.__walkLook; l.setPosition(10.9, 4.2); l.setYaw(0); l.setPitch(-0.02) })()
